pairs.subject: agent-runtime-assembly
pairs.evidence: crates/server/src/triggers.rs:384 A predicate hook can stop a hop, but if its contributed WASM plugin is missing, traps or returns garbage, the hop fires by default; the operator has to opt in to fail-closed with on_error=skip, which is the standard's 'skipped guard' failure mode (the code does report it at error level and in the ledger).

techniques.evidence: crates/server/src/triggers.rs:384 Intercepting (predicate) contributions fail open by default. The standard says an intercepting contribution is required unless the operator explicitly downgrades it.

crates/server/src/triggers.rs:749 post_enqueue is a pure observer whose output is discarded. predicate/transform form a closed mutator vocabulary (HookSlot), and a veto is a typed {pass:false} result, not a thrown error.

crates/server/src/triggers.rs:520 Hooks are placed by a declared slot class with a fixed host-owned order (predicate→transform→enqueue→post_enqueue), never by list index. The host writes every incident, vetoes included, to the ledger.

crates/server/src/triggers.rs:595 Every hook call is bounded by a wasm fuel/memory cap. Each slot's fail direction comes from its class (predicate per on_error, transform keeps the original envelope, post_enqueue affects nothing).
crates/server/src/triggers.rs:1176 A configured hook whose payload is not installed or not executable is reported at error level and gets a ledger row. A missing payload is loud, not silent.
crates/server/src/triggers.rs:360 Judged by analogy: a hop is a new job with its own id, and its parent is carried as a field plus depth/chain lineage. This is job-to-job, not agent-to-agent.

pairs.registryProposal: The fail-direction rule assumes an intercepting contribution guards safety. Here the predicate is a routing filter, and the repo deliberately prefers fail-open so that 'a broken plugin never wedges a pipeline edge'. The technique could say whether a contributed filter whose only cost on failure is extra work counts as intercepting.

pairs.subject: agent-runtime-assembly
pairs.evidence: crates/server/src/mcp/mod.rs:652 tools/list is built from AppState alone, so every MCP client is shown the `fetch` tool. tool_fetch then refuses any caller without a valid job token, so the roster and the run-time refusal are not derived from one policy on one session.

techniques.evidence: crates/server/src/mcp/mod.rs:652 `fetch` is a session-scoped capability that resolves from the job token on the request, but it sits on the default roster for every session. The allow_enqueue tools do derive roster and call gate from the same config switch (mod.rs:746).

crates/server/src/main.rs:308 The boot sweep sends every interrupted running job through fail(): it is either requeued or permanently `failed`, with the cause kept only as a reason string (FailReason::Text("interrupted at boot") in core storage). There is no first-class indeterminate status.

crates/server/src/registry.rs:263 Dynamic-app code loads only from the operator's [plugins] app_dir behind the [wasm_apps] startup switch. A load failure is a warning, and the module is listed as unrunnable with a reason instead of being skipped silently.
crates/server/src/registry.rs:300 Judged by analogy on the app-dispatch namespace: a contributed module can never shadow a compiled-in name. No contributed HTTP routes exist.
crates/server/src/registry.rs:379 Activation reads the payload's actual bytes against the reviewed catalog pin, not just the pointer. Unpinned modules still register but are marked pinned:false.

pairs.subject: agent-runtime-assembly
pairs.evidence: crates/server/src/routes/triggers.rs:296 TriggerPluginHooks has no deny_unknown_fields, so a misspelled slot key (e.g. "predicte") deserializes to all-None. This branch then stores the trigger as having no hooks and returns 201, so the gate is silently absent instead of the registration being refused.

techniques.evidence: crates/server/src/routes/triggers.rs:296 A registration naming an unknown hook point is silently dropped instead of refused. Compare watches.rs:347, which refuses a plugin sink naming an unloaded module.

crates/server/src/routes/triggers.rs:125 The service tier cannot load code (provisioner.rs:13 says promotion cannot shortcut the operator's catalog edit). But the trigger API accepts an intercepting predicate on an uninstalled plugin, and that predicate fails open by default.

crates/server/src/routes/triggers.rs:514 The dry-run is a separate check: it compares the declared hooks with what the host can actually execute and reports unusable_plugins (meaning the hop is ungated).
